title: Python Automation Toolkit
summary: Python scripts call APIs and cloud SDKs, run on schedule through cron or systemd or in CI, and produce reports and checks.

nodes.label: Scheduler / Trigger
nodes.detail: Starts scripts on a schedule or on events such as a pull request or webhook.

nodes.label: Python Script
nodes.detail: Uses argparse or click, reads configuration from environment variables, logs clearly and exits with meaningful codes.

nodes.label: Virtualenv
nodes.detail: Isolated environment with versions pinned in requirements, so runs are reproducible across machines.

nodes.label: API Client
nodes.detail: Calls REST APIs with timeouts, retries and authentication headers, and parses JSON responses.

nodes.label: boto3
nodes.detail: Lists and manages AWS resources using IAM roles, with paginators for large result sets.

nodes.label: Docker SDK
nodes.detail: Starts, inspects and cleans up containers and images programmatically.

nodes.label: CI Checks
nodes.detail: Runs pytest, linters and config validators on each change, failing the build on problems.

nodes.label: Reports / Alerts
nodes.detail: Writes summaries such as inventory or compliance reports and sends notifications or files for review.

steps.title: Trigger starts the script
steps.text: A cron entry, systemd timer or CI job runs the entry point inside a pinned virtualenv.

steps.title: Script calls integrations
steps.text: It uses HTTP clients, boto3 and the Docker SDK to gather or change state.

steps.title: Results are aggregated
steps.text: Responses are normalised into a summary with counts, errors and anomalies.

steps.title: CI guards the code
steps.text: Lint and tests run on each change so automation stays reliable.

steps.title: Report is delivered
steps.text: The report is written to a file or sent to chat, and exit codes show failures to the scheduler.
